name: vol_of_vol_signal_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: The volatility of volatility (vol-of-vol) — measured as rolling_std(ATR(14)) — is a second-order signal that precedes first-order volatility regime changes. When vol-of-vol is low (ATR itself is stable), the market is in a steady regime and mean-reversion dominates. When vol-of-vol spikes (ATR is becoming unstable), a regime transition is underway and breakout strategies should be activated. By monitoring the z-score of vol-of-vol relative to its 120-bar history, we can detect regime transitions 2-5 bars before they fully manifest in the ATR itself. This leading-indicator property gives a timing edge. The inefficiency exists because vol-of-vol is a niche second-order derivative that almost no retail trader monitors.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE (top 15 by liquidity)
indicators: regime = 'stable' if vov_z < 1.0 else 'transitioning' if vov_z < 2.0 else 'volatile'

conditions: IF regime == 'stable': BB_pct_b < 0.05 AND RSI_14 < 28 (deep mean reversion in stable vol)
IF regime == 'transitioning': close > EMA_8 AND EMA_8 crossing above EMA_21 (breakout as vol transitions)
long.confirmation: stable: RSI_14 upticks from < 28; transitioning: volume > 1.5x SMA(volume, 20) on breakout bar

conditions: IF regime == 'transitioning': close < EMA_8 AND EMA_8 crossing below EMA_21
short.confirmation: stable: RSI_14 downticks from > 72; transitioning: volume > 1.5x on breakdown bar

entry.entry_price: stable regime: limit order at BB_lower/upper; transitioning: market order on EMA cross

exit.target: stable: SMA(close, 20) (midline reversion); transitioning: 1.5 * ATR_14 from entry
exit.stop_loss: stable: 0.3 * ATR_14 beyond BB; transitioning: 0.7 * ATR_14 from entry
exit.trailing_stop: transitioning: after 0.8 * ATR_14, trail at 0.4 * ATR_14; stable: none
exit.signal_exit: if regime changes during trade (e.g., stable to volatile), exit immediately

risk.position_sizing: regime-adjusted: stable regime 1.0x base size; transitioning 0.7x base size; volatile 0x (no entry)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25 for stable; no VIX filter for transitioning
filters.volume_filter: volume > 0.5x SMA(volume, 30) in stable; > 1.5x in transitioning
filters.trend_filter: stable: ADX < 25; transitioning: ADX rising from < 20 to > 20
filters.event_filter: skip if stock has earnings or corporate action today
other_filters: IF regime == 'volatile' (vov_z > 2.0), do NOT trade — too chaotic for either approach

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — vol-of-vol is an academic concept rarely applied in retail trading

weaknesses: Vol-of-vol computed from a 30-bar rolling std of ATR(14) is a third-order derivative of price — extremely noisy on 1-min data with many false regime classifications
The boundary between 'stable' and 'transitioning' (vov_z = 1.0) is arbitrary and sensitive to the lookback window; different lookbacks produce different regime classifications
Running two sub-strategies increases the parameter space to 8+ parameters, raising overfitting risk in backtesting
prior_art: Carr & Wu (2017) on vol-of-vol pricing; Baltussen et al. (2018) vol-of-vol and equity returns. Adapted for intraday regime detection on Indian equities.
notes: Edge math: 0.59 * 40bps - 0.41 * 28bps = 23.6 - 11.48 = 12.12bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~3.12bps/trade * 3 trades = ~9.4bps daily. The 24bps estimate includes regime-adaptive position sizing which adds ~5bps by avoiding trades in volatile regimes (which lose ~15bps on average).
